output.target_audience: High school seniors or first-year university students

section_1.title: Introduction: Meet Robby the Robot
section_1.content: Introduce the two core perspectives of calculus through a character. Establish the concept of 'Rate of Change' vs. 'Total Accumulation' using a moving object. Explain that derivatives look at the 'now,' while integrals look at the 'sum'.
section_1.example: An animation of Robby the Robot walking. A 'Speedometer' above his head shows his derivative (velocity at an instant), while a 'Distance Tracker' bar at the bottom shows his integral (total distance covered over time).

section_2.title: Prerequisite Bridge: Slopes and Areas
section_2.content: Briefly revisit prerequisite geometry concepts. Define the derivative visually as the slope of a tangent line and the integral as the area under a curve. Use a simple linear graph to show how these two geometric properties relate to the same line.
section_2.example: A split-screen view: On the left, a magnifying glass zooms in on a curve to show a tiny straight line (Slope/Derivative). On the right, the space under the curve is filled with colorful vertical rectangles (Area/Integral).

section_3.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Undo
section_3.content: Explain the core discovery: Integration and Differentiation are inverse operations, much like addition and subtraction. If you start with a position, differentiate to get velocity, and then integrate that velocity, you return to the change in position.
section_3.example: A 'Function Machine' animation. Feed the function x² into the 'Derivative Shredder' to get 2x. Then, feed 2x into the 'Integral Glue Bottle' to see it reassembled back into x² (plus a constant 'C' represented by a mysterious mystery box).

section_4.title: Visualizing the Accumulation Function
section_4.content: Show how the area under a rate-of-change graph (the integral) builds up to create the original function's value. This section emphasizes the 'Area-so-far' concept to bridge the gap between a static graph and dynamic movement.
section_4.example: A graph of a constant velocity. As a slider moves along the x-axis (time), the area under the velocity line turns blue, and simultaneously, a second graph above it plots a rising line showing the total distance accumulated.

section_5.title: Real-World Application: The Leaky Water Tank
section_5.content: Apply the relationship to a physics scenario. Use the flow rate of water to determine the total volume, demonstrating how knowing the derivative (flow rate) allows us to reconstruct the state of the system (total volume) via integration.
section_5.example: A water tank with a hole. A gauge shows the 'Flow Rate' (liters per second). An animation shows that the 'Area' under the Flow Rate vs. Time graph exactly matches the total amount of water collected in a bucket below the tank.

section_6.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_6.content: Recap the 'Inverse Relationship'. Emphasize that the derivative breaks a whole down into tiny changes, while the integral builds those tiny changes back into a whole. Final visual confirmation of the symmetry.
section_6.example: A circular infographic showing an arrow pointing from 'Position' to 'Velocity' labeled 'Differentiate', and an arrow pointing back labeled 'Integrate', with Robby the Robot waving in the center.

Integrals measure the total distance Robby has traveled.
One looks at the 'now', the other the 'sum'.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.9
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.9
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout
        title_text = "Introduction: Meet Robby the Robot"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Meet Robby, our robotic guide to the world of calculus.",
            "Derivatives track Robby's speed at any single moment.",
            "Integrals measure the total distance Robby has traveled.",
            "One looks at the 'now', the other the 'sum'.",
            "Together, they reveal the hidden harmony of change."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Create Robby the Robot character
        robby_head = Rectangle(width=0.4, height=0.3, fill_opacity=1, color="#87CEEB")
        eye_l = Dot(radius=0.04, color=BLACK).move_to(robby_head.get_center() + LEFT*0.1 + UP*0.05)
        eye_r = Dot(radius=0.04, color=BLACK).move_to(robby_head.get_center() + RIGHT*0.1 + UP*0.05)
        robby_body = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.5, fill_opacity=1, color="#87CEEB").next_to(robby_head, DOWN, buff=0.05)
        wheel_l = Circle(radius=0.08, fill_opacity=1, color=GRAY).next_to(robby_body, DOWN, buff=0, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        wheel_r = Circle(radius=0.08, fill_opacity=1, color=GRAY).next_to(robby_body, DOWN, buff=0, aligned_edge=RIGHT)
        robby = VGroup(robby_head, eye_l, eye_r, robby_body, wheel_l, wheel_r)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color the active lecture line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Robby enters and walks across
        self.place_at_grid(robby, "D1")
        self.play(FadeIn(robby))
        self.play(robby.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"]), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Speedometer above Robby
        speed_circle = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI, color="#FFFF00")
        speed_needle = Line(speed_circle.get_center(), speed_circle.get_center() + UP*0.4, color=RED)
        speed_label = MathTex("v(t)", color="#FFFF00", font_size=24).next_to(speed_circle, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        speedometer = VGroup(speed_circle, speed_needle, speed_label)
        
        # Place Speedometer above Robby's path
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer, "B3")
        self.play(robby.animate.move_to(self.grid["D3"]))

        area_poly = Polygon(
            vel_axes.c2p(0, 0), vel_axes.c2p(0, 1.5), 
            vel_axes.c2p(0, 1.5), vel_axes.c2p(0, 0),
            color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=0
        )
        def update_area(p):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            p.set_points_as_corners([
                vel_axes.c2p(0, 0),
                vel_axes.c2p(0, 1.5),
                vel_axes.c2p(t, 1.5),
                vel_axes.c2p(t, 0)
            ])
        area_poly.add_updater(update_area)
        
        self.play(Create(vel_axes), Write(vel_label))
        self.play(Create(v_func))
        self.add(area_poly)
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2)

        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(dist_axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value(), 1.5 * time_tracker.get_value())))

        # Connecting Vertical Line

        def update_conn_line(l):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            p1 = dist_axes.c2p(t, 1.5 * t)
            p2 = vel_axes.c2p(t, 1.5)
            l.set_points_as_corners([p1, p2])

        )

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "Real-World Application: The Leaky Water Tank"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Consider water leaking from a tank at varying rates.",
            "The flow rate tells us the derivative of volume.",
            "Integrating that flow reveals the total water lost."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        TANK_COLOR = "#4682B4"
        BUCKET_COLOR = "#C0C0C0"
        FLOW_COLOR = "#FF4500"
        WATER_COLOR = "#87CEEB"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a blue water tank (#4682B4) leaking into a silver bucket (#C0C0C0).
        
        tank_body = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=2.0, color=TANK_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3)
        tank_label = Text("Water Tank", font_size=18, color=TANK_COLOR)
        tank_group = VGroup(tank_body, tank_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(tank_group, "A1", "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        bucket_body = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.5, height=1.5, color=BUCKET_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3)
        bucket_label = Text("Bucket", font_size=18, color=BUCKET_COLOR)
        bucket_group = VGroup(bucket_body, bucket_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(bucket_group, "E1", "F3", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Leak stream (connection between tank and bucket)
        stream = Line(tank_group.get_bottom(), bucket_group.get_top(), color=WATER_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(TANK_COLOR)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(tank_group),
            FadeIn(bucket_group),
            Create(stream),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Plot a red 'Flow Rate' curve (#FF4500) on a side graph.
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 2, 0.5],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE, "include_tip": True},
            tips=False
        )
        axes_labels = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="t", y_label="f(t)")
        flow_graph_group = VGroup(axes, axes_labels)
        self.place_in_area(flow_graph_group, "B4", "E6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        def flow_func(t):
            # A varying flow rate
            return 1 + 0.5 * np.sin(t)
            
        curve = axes.plot(flow_func, x_range=[0, 5], color=FLOW_COLOR)
        curve_label = Text("Flow Rate (f(t))", font_size=16, color=FLOW_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(FLOW_COLOR)
        self.play(
            Create(axes),
            Create(axes_labels),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            Create(curve),
            FadeIn(curve_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Sync the bucket filling with the area under the flow graph.
        
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Area under curve (Integral)
        area = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_area(
            curve, 
            x_range=[0, time_tracker.get_value()], 
            color=WATER_COLOR, 
            opacity=0.4
        ))
        
        # Integral of f(t) = 1 + 0.5 sin(t) is V(t) = t - 0.5 cos(t) + 0.5
        def integral_func(t):
            return t - 0.5 * np.cos(t) + 0.5
            
        max_integral = integral_func(5)
        
        # Water in the bucket
        bucket_water = Rectangle(
            width=bucket_body.width - 0.1,
            height=0.01,
            color=WATER_COLOR,
            fill_opacity=0.8,
            stroke_width=0
        )
        bucket_water.move_to(bucket_body.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        # Update water level in bucket based on the integral
        def update_water(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            current_volume = integral_func(t)
            # Map volume to height
            h = (current_volume / max_integral) * (bucket_body.height - 0.1)
            m.stretch_to_fit_height(max(h, 0.001))
            m.move_to(bucket_body.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            
        bucket_water.add_updater(update_water)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WATER_COLOR)
        self.add(area, bucket_water)
        
        # Fill both area and bucket simultaneously
        self.play(
            time_tracker.animate.set_value(5),
            run_time=6,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(2)

section_3.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Undo
section_3.content: Explain the core discovery: Integration and Differentiation are inverse operations, much like addition and subtraction. If you start with a position, differentiate to get velocity, and then integrate that velocity, you return to the change in position.

        curve = axes.plot(func, x_range=[0, 4], color=BLUE_CURVE)
        curve_label = MathTex("f(x)", color=BLUE_CURVE, font_size=24)

        # x_range is [0, 4], so alpha = x / 4.0
        tangent_line = TangentLine(curve, alpha=t.get_value() / 4.0, length=2.5, color=RED_TANGENT)
        dot = Dot(axes.c2p(t.get_value(), func(t.get_value())), color=RED_TANGENT)

            new_line = TangentLine(curve, alpha=t.get_value() / 4.0, length=2.5, color=RED_TANGENT)
            mob.become(new_line)
            
        def update_dot(mob):
            mob.move_to(axes.c2p(t.get_value(), func(t.get_value())))

        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)
        dot.add_updater(update_dot)

        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        # Velocity function: v(t) = 1.5
        v_func = vel_axes.plot(lambda t: 1.5, x_range=[0, 3.5], color=ORANGE)
        
        # Tracker for slider/time
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Area under velocity (persistent)
        # We define a polygon that starts as a thin line at x=0
        area_poly = Polygon(
            vel_axes.c2p(0, 0), vel_axes.c2p(0, 1.5), 
            vel_axes.c2p(0, 1.5), vel_axes.c2p(0, 0),
            color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=0
        )
        def update_area(p):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            p.set_points_as_corners([
                vel_axes.c2p(0, 0),
                vel_axes.c2p(0, 1.5),
                vel_axes.c2p(t, 1.5),
                vel_axes.c2p(t, 0)
            ])
        area_poly.add_updater(update_area)
        
        self.play(Create(vel_axes), Write(vel_label))
        self.play(Create(v_func))
        self.add(area_poly)
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2)

        self.place_in_area(dist_group, "A3", "C6")
        
        # Distance point and trace
        # d(t) = 1.5 * t (integral of 1.5)
        dot = Dot(color=GREEN, radius=0.08)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(dist_axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value(), 1.5 * time_tracker.get_value())))
        path = TracedPath(dot.get_center, stroke_color=GREEN, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(Create(dist_axes), Write(dist_label))
        self.add(path, dot)

            p1 = dist_axes.c2p(t, 1.5 * t)

        self.place_in_area(flow_graph_group, "B4", "E6", scale_factor=0.9)

            height=0.01,
            color=WATER_COLOR,
            fill_opacity=0.8,
            stroke_width=0
        )
        bucket_water.move_to(bucket_body.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        # Update water level in bucket based on the integral
        def update_water(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            current_volume = integral_func(t)
            # Map volume to height
            h = (current_volume / max_integral) * (bucket_body.height - 0.1)
            m.stretch_to_fit_height(max(h, 0.001))
            m.move_to(bucket_body.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            
        bucket_water.add_updater(update_water)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WATER_COLOR)
        self.add(area, bucket_water)
        
        # Fill both area and bucket simultaneously
        self.play(
            time_tracker.animate.set_value(5),
            run_time=6,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup
        title_text = "Visualizing the Accumulation Function"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine area building up as we move along time.",
            "This growing area creates a new 'accumulation function'.",
            "The rate of this growth is the original curve."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        ORANGE = "#FFA500"
        BLUE = "#ADD8E6"
        GREEN = "#00FF00"
        YELLOW_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Imagine area building up as we move along time."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Velocity Axes (Bottom Area: D3 to F6)
        vel_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1], 
            y_range=[0, 2, 1], 
            x_length=3.5, 
            y_length=2,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 18}
        )
        vel_label = Text("Velocity (v)", font_size=20, color=ORANGE)
        vel_group = VGroup(vel_axes, vel_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(vel_group, "D3", "F6")
        
        # Velocity function: v(t) = 1.5
        v_func = vel_axes.plot(lambda t: 1.5, x_range=[0, 3.5], color=ORANGE)
        
        # Tracker for slider/time
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Area under velocity (persistent)
        # We define a polygon that starts as a thin line at x=0
        area_poly = Polygon(
            vel_axes.c2p(0, 0), vel_axes.c2p(0, 1.5), 
            vel_axes.c2p(0, 1.5), vel_axes.c2p(0, 0),
            color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=0
        )
        def update_area(p):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            p.set_points_as_corners([
                vel_axes.c2p(0, 0),
                vel_axes.c2p(0, 1.5),

                vel_axes.c2p(t, 0)
            ])

        self.play(Create(vel_axes), Write(vel_label))
        self.play(Create(v_func))
        self.add(area_poly)
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "This growing area creates a new 'accumulation function'."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Distance Axes (Top Area: A3 to C6)
        dist_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1], 
            y_range=[0, 6, 2], 
            x_length=3.5, 
            y_length=2,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 18}
        )
        dist_label = Text("Distance (s)", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        dist_group = VGroup(dist_axes, dist_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(dist_group, "A3", "C6")
        
        # Distance point and trace
        # d(t) = 1.5 * t (integral of 1.5)
        dot = Dot(color=GREEN, radius=0.08)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(dist_axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value(), 1.5 * time_tracker.get_value())))
        path = TracedPath(dot.get_center, stroke_color=GREEN, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(Create(dist_axes), Write(dist_label))
        self.add(path, dot)
        
        # Reset and flow to show synchronized growth
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(0), run_time=1)
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(3.5), run_time=4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The rate of this growth is the original curve."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW_HIGHLIGHT)
        
        # Connecting Vertical Line
        conn_line = Line(ORIGIN, UP, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).set_stroke(opacity=0.6)
        def update_conn_line(l):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            p1 = dist_axes.c2p(t, 1.5 * t)
            p2 = vel_axes.c2p(t, 1.5)
            l.set_points_as_corners([p1, p2])
        conn_line.add_updater(update_conn_line)
        
        # Indicators: Numerical values for Area and Distance
        area_val_label = VGroup(
            Text("Area:", font_size=18, color=BLUE),
            DecimalNumber(0, font_size=18, color=BLUE)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        dist_val_label = VGroup(
            Text("Dist:", font_size=18, color=GREEN),
            DecimalNumber(0, font_size=18, color=GREEN)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Positioning indicators next to the graphs
        self.place_at_grid(area_val_label, "E2")
        self.place_at_grid(dist_val_label, "B2")
        
        area_val_label[1].add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(1.5 * time_tracker.get_value()))
        dist_val_label[1].add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(1.5 * time_tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.add(conn_line)
        self.play(Write(area_val_label), Write(dist_val_label))
        
        # Final scrub to demonstrate the rate of growth connection
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=2)
        self.play(time_tracker.animate.set_value(3.2), run_time=2)
        
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "Real-World Application: The Leaky Water Tank"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Consider water leaking from a tank at varying rates.",
            "The flow rate tells us the derivative of volume.",
            "Integrating that flow reveals the total water lost."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        TANK_COLOR = "#4682B4"
        BUCKET_COLOR = "#C0C0C0"
        FLOW_COLOR = "#FF4500"
        WATER_COLOR = "#87CEEB"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a blue water tank (#4682B4) leaking into a silver bucket (#C0C0C0).
        
        tank_body = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=2.0, color=TANK_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3)
        tank_label = Text("Water Tank", font_size=18, color=TANK_COLOR)
        tank_group = VGroup(tank_body, tank_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(tank_group, "A1", "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        bucket_body = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.5, height=1.5, color=BUCKET_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3)
        bucket_label = Text("Bucket", font_size=18, color=BUCKET_COLOR)
        bucket_group = VGroup(bucket_body, bucket_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(bucket_group, "E1", "F3", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Leak stream (connection between tank and bucket)
        stream = Line(tank_group.get_bottom(), bucket_group.get_top(), color=WATER_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(TANK_COLOR)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(tank_group),
            FadeIn(bucket_group),
            Create(stream),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Plot a red 'Flow Rate' curve (#FF4500) on a side graph.
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 2, 0.5],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE, "include_tip": True},
            tips=False
        )
        axes_labels = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="t", y_label="f(t)")
        flow_graph_group = VGroup(axes, axes_labels)
        self.place_in_area(flow_graph_group, "B4", "E6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        def flow_func(t):
            # A varying flow rate
            return 1 + 0.5 * np.sin(t)
            
        curve = axes.plot(flow_func, x_range=[0, 5], color=FLOW_COLOR)
        curve_label = Text("Flow Rate (f(t))", font_size=16, color=FLOW_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(FLOW_COLOR)
        self.play(
            Create(axes),
            Create(axes_labels),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            Create(curve),
            FadeIn(curve_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Sync the bucket filling with the area under the flow graph.
        
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Area under curve (Integral)
        area = always_redraw(lambda: axes.get_area(
            curve, 
            x_range=[0, time_tracker.get_value()], 
            color=WATER_COLOR, 
            opacity=0.4
        ))
        
        # Integral of f(t) = 1 + 0.5 sin(t) is V(t) = t - 0.5 cos(t) + 0.5
        def integral_func(t):
            return t - 0.5 * np.cos(t) + 0.5
            
        max_integral = integral_func(5)
        
        # Water in the bucket
        bucket_water = Rectangle(
            width=bucket_body.width - 0.1,
            height=0.01,
            color=WATER_COLOR,
            fill_opacity=0.8,
            stroke_width=0
        )
        bucket_water.move_to(bucket_body.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        # Update water level in bucket based on the integral
        def update_water(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            current_volume = integral_func(t)
            # Map volume to height
            h = (current_volume / max_integral) * (bucket_body.height - 0.1)
            m.stretch_to_fit_height(max(h, 0.001))
            m.move_to(bucket_body.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            
        bucket_water.add_updater(update_water)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WATER_COLOR)
        self.add(area, bucket_water)
        
        # Fill both area and bucket simultaneously
        self.play(
            time_tracker.animate.set_value(5),
            run_time=6,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(2)

                "- These geometric properties are two sides of one coin."
            ]
        )
        
        # Colors defined in animation description and script
        BLUE_CURVE = "#1E90FF"
        RED_TANGENT = "#FF0000"
        YELLOW_RECTS = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Script: "A derivative is the slope of a tangent line."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(RED_TANGENT)
        
        # Define Axes on the grid
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # f(x) = 0.5 * (x - 2)^2 + 1
        func = lambda x: 0.5 * (x - 2)**2 + 1
        curve = axes.plot(func, x_range=[0, 4], color=BLUE_CURVE)
        curve_label = MathTex("f(x)", color=BLUE_CURVE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)

        # Tangent Logic using ValueTracker and Updaters for efficiency
        t = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        # Replace axes.get_tangent_line (which doesn't exist) with TangentLine class
        # x_range is [0, 4], so alpha = x / 4.0
        tangent_line = TangentLine(curve, alpha=t.get_value() / 4.0, length=2.5, color=RED_TANGENT)
        dot = Dot(axes.c2p(t.get_value(), func(t.get_value())), color=RED_TANGENT)
        
        # Define Updaters to update mobjects in-place
        def update_tangent(mob):
            new_line = TangentLine(curve, alpha=t.get_value() / 4.0, length=2.5, color=RED_TANGENT)
            mob.become(new_line)
            
        def update_dot(mob):
            mob.move_to(axes.c2p(t.get_value(), func(t.get_value())))

        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)
        dot.add_updater(update_dot)

        # Initial drawing
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), Write(curve_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Create(tangent_line), Create(dot))
        
        # Animate tangent sliding along the curve
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(3.5), run_time=3, rate_func=there_and_back)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Script: "An integral is the area trapped under a curve."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW_RECTS)
        
        # Create Riemann Rectangles to represent the integral
        rects = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(
            curve, 
            x_range=[0.5, 3.5], 
            dx=0.3, 
            fill_opacity=0.6, 
            stroke_width=0.1, 
            color=YELLOW_RECTS
        )
        
        self.play(Create(rects), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Script: "These geometric properties are two sides of one coin."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GOLD)
        
        # Move the tangent line and rectangles together to emphasize connection
        self.play(
            t.animate.set_value(2),
            rects.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.8),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.content: Introduce the two core perspectives of calculus through a character. Establish the concept of 'Rate of Change' vs. 'Total Accumulation' using a moving object. Explain that derivatives look at the 'now,' while integrals look at the 'sum'.

outline.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Undo
outline.content: Explain the core discovery: Integration and Differentiation are inverse operations, much like addition and subtraction. If you start with a position, differentiate to get velocity, and then integrate that velocity, you return to the change in position.
outline.example: A 'Function Machine' animation. Feed the function x² into the 'Derivative Shredder' to get 2x. Then, feed 2x into the 'Integral Glue Bottle' to see it reassembled back into x² (plus a constant 'C' represented by a mysterious mystery box).

storyboard.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Undo
lecture_lines: Calculus has a secret: these operations are inverse partners.
Differentiation breaks a function down into its rate.
Integration acts like glue, rebuilding the original whole.
Start with position, differentiate, then integrate to return home.
This 'Great Undo' is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
animations: Animate 'x^2' entering a grey machine (#A9A9A9) labeled 'd/dx'.
The machine outputs '2x' in a vibrant purple color (#800080).
'2x' enters a second machine labeled with an integral sign '∫'.
The machine outputs 'x^2 + C' in green (#00FF00).
Flash 'Inverse Operations' in white (#FFFFFF) across the center.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "Real-World Application: The Leaky Water Tank"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Consider water leaking from a tank at varying rates.",
            "The flow rate tells us the derivative of volume.",
            "Integrating that flow reveals the total water lost."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        TANK_COLOR = "#4682B4"
        BUCKET_COLOR = "#C0C0C0"
        FLOW_COLOR = "#FF4500"
        WATER_COLOR = "#87CEEB"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a blue water tank [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tank.svg] (#4682B4) 
        # leaking into a silver bucket (#C0C0C0).
        
        # Resolve Issue 21: Load SVG asset
        tank_svg = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tank.svg")
        tank_svg.set_color(TANK_COLOR)
        tank_label = Text("Water Tank", font_size=18, color=TANK_COLOR)
        tank_group = VGroup(tank_svg, tank_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Resolve Issue 31: Place in B1-C3 instead of A1-B3
        self.place_in_area(tank_group, "B1", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        bucket_body = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.5, height=1.5, color=BUCKET_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3)
        bucket_label = Text("Bucket", font_size=18, color=BUCKET_COLOR)
        bucket_group = VGroup(bucket_body, bucket_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # Resolve Issue 33: Place in D1-E3 instead of E1-F3
        self.place_in_area(bucket_group, "D1", "E3", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Leak stream (connection between tank and bucket)
        stream = Line(tank_group.get_bottom(), bucket_group.get_top(), color=WATER_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(TANK_COLOR)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(tank_group),
            FadeIn(bucket_group),
            Create(stream),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Plot a red 'Flow Rate' curve (#FF4500) on a side graph.
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 2, 0.5],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE, "include_tip": True},
            tips=False
        )
        axes_labels = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="t", y_label="f(t)")
        flow_graph_group = VGroup(axes, axes_labels)
        
        # Resolve Issue 32: scale_factor=0.8 instead of 0.9
        self.place_in_area(flow_graph_group, "B4", "E6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        def flow_func(t):
            # A varying flow rate
            return 1 + 0.5 * np.sin(t)
            
        curve = axes.plot(flow_func, x_range=[0, 5], color=FLOW_COLOR)
        curve_label = Text("Flow Rate (f(t))", font_size=16, color=FLOW_COLOR)
        # Position label relative to the grid
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(FLOW_COLOR)
        self.play(
            Create(axes),
            Create(axes_labels),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            Create(curve),
            FadeIn(curve_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Sync the bucket filling with the area under the flow graph.
        
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Area under curve (Integral)
        # Using a polygon update instead of always_redraw for consistency with instructions
        area = Polygon(
            axes.c2p(0, 0),
            axes.c2p(0, flow_func(0)),
            axes.c2p(0, 0),
            color=WATER_COLOR, 
            fill_opacity=0.4,
            stroke_width=0
        )
        
        def update_area(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            if t <= 0.01:
                return
            points = [axes.c2p(0, 0)]
            # Sample points for the curve area
            for x_val in np.linspace(0, t, 30):
                points.append(axes.c2p(x_val, flow_func(x_val)))
            points.append(axes.c2p(t, 0))
            m.set_points_as_corners(points)
            
        area.add_updater(update_area)
        
        # Integral of f(t) = 1 + 0.5 sin(t) is V(t) = t - 0.5 cos(t) + 0.5
        def integral_func(t):
            return t - 0.5 * np.cos(t) + 0.5
            
        max_integral = integral_func(5)
        
        # Water in the bucket
        bucket_water = Rectangle(
            width=bucket_body.width - 0.1,
            height=0.01,
            color=WATER_COLOR,
            fill_opacity=0.8,
            stroke_width=0
        )
        bucket_water.move_to(bucket_body.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        # Update water level in bucket based on the integral
        def update_water(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            current_volume = integral_func(t)
            # Map volume to height
            h = (current_volume / max_integral) * (bucket_body.height - 0.1)
            m.stretch_to_fit_height(max(h, 0.001))
            m.move_to(bucket_body.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            
        bucket_water.add_updater(update_water)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WATER_COLOR)
        self.add(area, bucket_water)
        
        # Fill both area and bucket simultaneously
        self.play(
            time_tracker.animate.set_value(5),
            run_time=6,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(2)

            ]

        # Define Updaters to update mobjects in-place without heavy redraws
        def update_tangent(mob):
            new_line = TangentLine(curve, alpha=t.get_value() / 4.0, length=2.5, color=RED_TANGENT)
            mob.become(new_line)
            
        def update_dot(mob):
            mob.move_to(axes.c2p(t.get_value(), func(t.get_value())))

        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)
        dot.add_updater(update_dot)

        # Initial drawing

            dx=0.3, 
            fill_opacity=0.6, 
            stroke_width=0.1, 
            color=YELLOW_RECTS
        )
        
        self.play(Create(rects), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Script: "These geometric properties are two sides of one coin."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(CONNECTION_COLOR)
        
        # Move the tangent line and rectangles together to emphasize connection
        # Return tangent to a central position and highlight area
        self.play(

            rects.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.8),

        )

            ]
        )

        axes = Axes(

            y_length=4,

        )

        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # f(x) = 0.5 * (x - 2)^2 + 1
        func = lambda x: 0.5 * (x - 2)**2 + 1
        curve = axes.plot(func, x_range=[0, 4], color=BLUE_CURVE)
        
        # Addressing Issue #27: Move curve label to B6 to avoid overlap with shifted axes
        curve_label = MathTex("f(x)", color=BLUE_CURVE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, 'B6', scale_factor=0.8)

        # Tangent Logic using ValueTracker and Updaters for efficiency
        t = ValueTracker(0.5)
        
        # Create persistent tangent line and dot
        tangent_line = TangentLine(curve, alpha=t.get_value() / 4.0, length=2.5, color=RED_TANGENT)
        dot = Dot(axes.c2p(t.get_value(), func(t.get_value())), color=RED_TANGENT)
        
        # Define Updaters to update mobjects in-place without heavy redraws
        def update_tangent(mob):
            new_line = TangentLine(curve, alpha=t.get_value() / 4.0, length=2.5, color=RED_TANGENT)
            mob.become(new_line)
            
        def update_dot(mob):
            mob.move_to(axes.c2p(t.get_value(), func(t.get_value())))

        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)
        dot.add_updater(update_dot)

        # Initial drawing
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), Write(curve_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Create(tangent_line), Create(dot))
        
        # Animate tangent sliding along the curve
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(3.5), run_time=3, rate_func=there_and_back)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Script: "An integral is the area trapped under a curve."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW_RECTS)
        
        # Create Riemann Rectangles to represent the integral
        rects = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(
            curve, 
            x_range=[0.5, 3.5], 
            dx=0.3, 
            fill_opacity=0.6, 
            stroke_width=0.1, 
            color=YELLOW_RECTS
        )
        
        self.play(Create(rects), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Script: "These geometric properties are two sides of one coin."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(CONNECTION_COLOR)
        
        # Move the tangent line and rectangles together to emphasize connection
        # Return tangent to a central position and highlight area
        self.play(
            t.animate.set_value(2),
            rects.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.8),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

    def construct(self):
        title_text = "Real-World Application: The Leaky Water Tank"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Consider water leaking from a tank at varying rates.",
            "The flow rate tells us the derivative of volume.",
            "Integrating that flow reveals the total water lost."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        TANK_COLOR = "#4682B4"
        BUCKET_COLOR = "#C0C0C0"
        FLOW_COLOR = "#FF4500"
        WATER_COLOR = "#87CEEB"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a blue water tank [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tank.svg] (#4682B4) 
        # leaking into a silver bucket (#C0C0C0).
        
        # Resolve Issue 21: Load SVG asset
        tank_svg = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tank.svg")
        tank_svg.set_color(TANK_COLOR)
        tank_label = Text("Water Tank", font_size=18, color=TANK_COLOR)
        tank_group = VGroup(tank_svg, tank_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Resolve Issue 31: Place in B1-C3 instead of A1-B3
        self.place_in_area(tank_group, "B1", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        bucket_body = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.5, height=1.5, color=BUCKET_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3)
        bucket_label = Text("Bucket", font_size=18, color=BUCKET_COLOR)
        bucket_group = VGroup(bucket_body, bucket_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # Resolve Issue 33: Place in D1-E3 instead of E1-F3
        self.place_in_area(bucket_group, "D1", "E3", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Leak stream (connection between tank and bucket)
        stream = Line(tank_group.get_bottom(), bucket_group.get_top(), color=WATER_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(TANK_COLOR)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(tank_group),
            FadeIn(bucket_group),
            Create(stream),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Plot a red 'Flow Rate' curve (#FF4500) on a side graph.
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 2, 0.5],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"color": WHITE, "include_tip": True},
            tips=False
        )
        axes_labels = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="t", y_label="f(t)")
        flow_graph_group = VGroup(axes, axes_labels)
        
        # Resolve Issue 32: scale_factor=0.8 instead of 0.9
        self.place_in_area(flow_graph_group, "B4", "E6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        def flow_func(t):
            # A varying flow rate
            return 1 + 0.5 * np.sin(t)
            
        curve = axes.plot(flow_func, x_range=[0, 5], color=FLOW_COLOR)
        curve_label = Text("Flow Rate (f(t))", font_size=16, color=FLOW_COLOR)
        # Position label relative to the grid
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(FLOW_COLOR)
        self.play(
            Create(axes),
            Create(axes_labels),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(
            Create(curve),
            FadeIn(curve_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Sync the bucket filling with the area under the flow graph.
        
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Area under curve (Integral)
        # Using a polygon update instead of always_redraw for consistency with instructions
        area = Polygon(
            axes.c2p(0, 0),
            axes.c2p(0, flow_func(0)),
            axes.c2p(0, 0),
            color=WATER_COLOR, 
            fill_opacity=0.4,
            stroke_width=0
        )
        
        def update_area(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            if t <= 0.01:
                return
            points = [axes.c2p(0, 0)]
            # Sample points for the curve area
            for x_val in np.linspace(0, t, 30):
                points.append(axes.c2p(x_val, flow_func(x_val)))
            points.append(axes.c2p(t, 0))
            m.set_points_as_corners(points)
            
        area.add_updater(update_area)
        
        # Integral of f(t) = 1 + 0.5 sin(t) is V(t) = t - 0.5 cos(t) + 0.5
        def integral_func(t):
            return t - 0.5 * np.cos(t) + 0.5
            
        max_integral = integral_func(5)
        
        # Water in the bucket
        bucket_water = Rectangle(
            width=bucket_body.width - 0.1,
            height=0.01,
            color=WATER_COLOR,
            fill_opacity=0.8,
            stroke_width=0
        )
        bucket_water.move_to(bucket_body.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        # Update water level in bucket based on the integral
        def update_water(m):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            current_volume = integral_func(t)
            # Map volume to height
            h = (current_volume / max_integral) * (bucket_body.height - 0.1)
            m.stretch_to_fit_height(max(h, 0.001))
            m.move_to(bucket_body.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
            
        bucket_water.add_updater(update_water)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WATER_COLOR)
        self.add(area, bucket_water)
        
        # Fill both area and bucket simultaneously
        self.play(
            time_tracker.animate.set_value(5),
            run_time=6,
            rate_func=linear
        )

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        # Setup
        title_text = "Visualizing the Accumulation Function"
        lecture_lines = [

            "This growing area creates a new 'accumulation function'.",
            "The rate of this growth is the original curve."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        ORANGE = "#FFA500"
        BLUE = "#ADD8E6"
        GREEN = "#00FF00"
        
        # Trackers
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Imagine area building up as we move along time."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        
        # Velocity Axes (Bottom Area: D4 to F6)

            x_range=[0, 4, 1], 
            y_range=[0, 2, 1], 
            x_length=3.0, 
            y_length=1.8,

        )
        vel_label = Text("Velocity (v)", font_size=18, color=ORANGE)

        self.place_in_area(vel_group, "D4", "F6")
        
        # Velocity function: v(t) = 1.5
        v_func = vel_axes.plot(lambda t: 1.5, x_range=[0, 3.5], color=ORANGE)
        
        # Area under velocity (persistent)
        area_poly = VMobject(fill_opacity=0.5, color=BLUE, stroke_width=0)
        def update_area(p):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            safe_t = max(t, 0.001)
            p.set_points_as_corners([
                vel_axes.c2p(0, 0),
                vel_axes.c2p(0, 1.5),
                vel_axes.c2p(safe_t, 1.5),
                vel_axes.c2p(safe_t, 0)
            ])
        area_poly.add_updater(update_area)

        # Slider asset (Issue 20)
        slider = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slider.svg")
        slider.scale(0.15).set_color(WHITE)
        slider.add_updater(lambda s: s.move_to(vel_axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value(), 0)))

        self.play(Create(v_func))
        self.add(area_poly, slider)

        # Distance Axes (Top Area: A4 to C6)

            x_range=[0, 4, 1], 
            y_range=[0, 6, 2],

            y_length=1.8,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "font_size": 16}
        )
        dist_label = Text("Distance (s)", font_size=18, color=GREEN)

        self.place_in_area(dist_group, "A4", "C6")
        
        # Distance graph (s(t) = 1.5 * t)

        def update_dist_line(l):
            t = time_tracker.get_value()
            if t < 0.01:
                l.set_points_as_corners([dist_axes.c2p(0, 0), dist_axes.c2p(0.01, 1.5*0.01)])
            else:
                l.set_points_as_corners([dist_axes.c2p(x, 1.5*x) for x in np.linspace(0, t, 30)])
        dist_line.add_updater(update_dist_line)

        # Vehicle asset (Issue 20)
        vehicle = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vehicle.svg")
        vehicle.scale(0.2).set_color(GREEN)
        vehicle.add_updater(lambda v: v.move_to(dist_axes.c2p(time_tracker.get_value(), 1.5 * time_tracker.get_value()) + UP*0.25))

        # Numerical indicators moved to column 3 (Issue 38)
        area_val_label = VGroup(
            Text("Area:", font_size=16, color=BLUE),
            DecimalNumber(0, font_size=16, color=BLUE)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        dist_val_label = VGroup(
            Text("Dist:", font_size=16, color=GREEN),
            DecimalNumber(0, font_size=16, color=GREEN)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(area_val_label, "E3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(dist_val_label, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Update values efficiently
        area_val_label[1].add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(1.5 * time_tracker.get_value()))
        dist_val_label[1].add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(1.5 * time_tracker.get_value()))

        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(ORANGE)

            l.set_points_as_corners([p1, p2])
        conn_line.add_updater(update_conn_line)
